title: Pulled Pork Stuffed Peppers
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot), grams derived FROM the printed measure via db\densities.json so the two agree by construction; quantities quantized to house quarters, drift noted per line where it exceeds 5%. Serving anchor: source serving is 1/2 stuffed pepper; 14 servings = 7 peppers, 14 halves.

ruled_substitutions.source: 1 1/2 cups Gouda cheese (6 oz) (or use cheddar)
ruled_substitutions.ruling: cheddar, taken from the page's OWN printed alternative '(or use cheddar)'. Gouda has no vocab row and no board commodity (vocab exit 3, nearest rows are different cheeses); the author sanctioned the swap in the ingredient line itself, so this is not a mapper guess. Macro delta gouda->cheddar is ~+3 cal/serving on labels.

ruled_substitutions.source: 1/3 cup Sugar-free BBQ sauce (or your favorite)
ruled_substitutions.ruling: regular BBQ Sauce, taken from the page's OWN printed alternative '(or your favorite)' (the page note says the author used a prepackaged keto sauce 'for convenience, but you can make your own if you prefer'). Sugar-Free BBQ Sauce has no vocab row and no board commodity. The swap is honestly booked at the regular-sauce label: +10.2 g carbs/serving vs the source's sugar-free figure, moving our carbs to 17.4 g - still comfortably under the 35 g gate. NOT silently priced at sugar-free macros.

Green Bell Peppers: the page specifies no color anywhere (re-verified on the live page 2026-08-16), the unmarked US retail default for 'bell pepper' is green, and green is the base price class - booking red or yellow pricing for an unspecified pepper would be the variety-pricing stretch the standing rejections forbid, in the expensive direction. Noted for QA: a reader who buys red pays more than the card's estimate.

ingredients.buy: 7 bell peppers (about 3 1/2 lb), halved and seeded
ingredients.notes: WEIGHT-ANCHORED by the author's parenthetical (2 large = about 1 lb, i.e. 227 g each - bigger than the densities each=120 medium): 1 lb x 3.5 = 3.5 lb = 1587.6 g; printed weight and grams agree, pepper count kept at the serving anchor's 7. DB row 24 cal/119 g. green-bell-pepper commodity exists but STILL has no priced board cell (CAPTURE verdict, 8 candidates across 6 stores - same state philly-cheesesteak-stuffed-peppers found); term enqueued BLOCKING, queue dedupes onto the existing item. Halving/seeding step missing from source instructions is noted by extraction; the buy string restores it.

ingredients.buy: 4 1/2 lb pork shoulder, cooked and pulled (about 8 1/2 cups; makes the 2 5/8 lb pulled pork the pot needs)
ingredients.notes: Standing canon maps 'pulled pork' -> Pork Shoulder. Source is COOKED weight (12 oz x 3.5 = 42 oz = 1190.7 g cooked, 8.5 cups at densities Pork Shoulder cup=140); converted to RAW purchase at a 60% pulled yield -> 1984.7 g raw, quantized 4 1/2 lb = 2041.2 g (+2.8%), and grams book the RAW weight against the raw USDA lean-and-fat DB row (186 cal / 17.4 P per 100 g) so cost and macros share one basis (chicken-bacon-ranch precedent). The 60% yield is VALIDATED by the source's own label, not assumed: at 60% recomputed protein lands +6.6% of their published 33.4 g; at 70% it lands -8%, at 50% it breaches +16.5%. Sensitivity across 50-70% spans 460-560 cal/serving - every reading inside the band, so the yield choice is not band-deciding. Board 7 of 7, cheapest Sam's $1.94/lb.

ingredients.source_raw: 1 1/2 cups Gouda cheese (6 oz) (or use cheddar)
ingredients.notes: printed alternative taken (see ruled_substitutions). WEIGHT-ANCHORED by the source's own parenthetical (6 oz): 21 oz = 595.4 g; cups follow at the label 1/4 cup = 28 g (5.25 cups). DB row 'Cheddar Cheese, Shredded' (GV label 110 cal / 6 P per 28 g). bid from the vocab row (cheddar-cheese); note the TERM resolver answers via the shredded-cheese commodity instead (include pattern), 7 of 7, cheapest Sam's $0.1521/oz - same resolver-vs-map split turkey-zucchini-noodle-casserole recorded for mozzarella.

ingredients.source_raw: 1/3 cup Sugar-free BBQ sauce (or your favorite)
ingredients.notes: printed alternative taken (see ruled_substitutions). Exact 1.17 cups quantized to 1 1/4 cups (+7.1% drift, noted) x densities cup=285 g = 356.25 g. Booked at the regular-sauce USDA row (172 cal / 40 C per 100 g) - the carb cost of the swap is taken honestly, not hidden. Board 7 of 7, cheapest Sam's $0.07/oz.

OPTIONAL garnish (extraction marked it optional; 'Garnish with cilantro' step). Exact 7 tbsp x densities tbsp=1 g = 7 g, ~0 macro. Board 5 of 7, cheapest Aldi $0.89/each. Not enqueued as blocking anywhere; answers from disk anyway.

pricing_terms_needed.why: the vessel of the dish, 7 peppers / 3.5 lb; commodity id exists but has NO priced board cell (CAPTURE verdict, 8 candidates across 6 stores); queue dedupes onto the existing philly-cheesesteak-stuffed-peppers item

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS on the protein instrument (+6.6%), which also validates the pulled-pork 60% cooked-to-raw yield (see the pork line). The calorie and carb gaps are fully accounted for by two DISCLOSED substitutions, both in the honest direction: regular BBQ sauce for the author's keto sugar-free sauce (+10.2 g carbs, ~+41 cal/serving - the entire 7 -> 17.4 carb move) and raw-basis lean-and-fat pork vs their cooked-basis figure (the flank-steak precedent gap direction). Neither is a portion error; portions are weight-anchored on all three macro-bearing lines (1 lb peppers, 12 oz pork, 6 oz cheese).
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 504.9 cal in [400, 650] PASS; carbs 17.4 g <= 35 PASS. Optional cilantro adds ~0.1 cal/serving.

loud_flags: Recipe parks in 'pricing' on the single green-bell-pepper term - the same unpriced-commodity state philly-cheesesteak-stuffed-peppers hit; one pricer ruling clears both recipes.

Bell pepper color is UNSPECIFIED by the source (page re-checked); booked green as the base variety per the ruling. If QA or the writer prefers 'any color' phrasing on the card, the cost estimate stays green-based.
Published card carbs will read ~17 g, not the source's 7 g, because we book regular BBQ sauce off the page's '(or your favorite)'; do not copy the source's 5-net-carb claim onto the card.
